title: Sep 18 Results + Sep 19 Preview: Two-Thirds Hit Rate With Strong Confidence Calibration
summary: Model posted 10-5 record on Sep 18, 66.7% accuracy with strong performance in 60%+ confidence tier

content.value:
## Sep 18 Results: Regression to Expected Value

The model delivered a solid 10-5 performance on September 18th, translating to a 66.7% hit rate that aligns closely with our confidence-weighted expectations. When we decompose the results by confidence tier, we see excellent calibration: picks with 60%+ confidence went 4-1, while our lower-confidence selections showed the expected variance.

## Key Takeaways: Confidence Calibration Success

The three misses came in our mid-confidence range (54-59%), which is exactly where we expect the highest variance. The Cubs-Reds result was essentially a coin flip gone wrong, while the Rays loss against the Sox represented a moderate upset. Most importantly, our highest-confidence pick—the Braves at 63%—delivered as projected.

From a WAR-adjusted perspective, the Guardians and Mariners victories were particularly valuable, as both came against teams with significantly worse run differentials. The model's ability to identify these mismatches while maintaining conservative confidence intervals demonstrates proper Bayesian updating.

## Sep 19 Preview: Tigers Return to South Side

Tomorrow's top-rated selection brings Detroit back to Chicago for another crack at the White Sox. At 62% confidence, this pick sits in our high-value tier based on starting pitcher differential and contextual factors.

## Matchup Analysis: Jobe's Peripheral Metrics Edge

Jackson Jobe brings superior strikeout and walk rates into this matchup, while Sean Burke has struggled with hard contact rates over his recent sample. The Tigers also maintain a significant advantage in team wRC+ over the past 30 days, though we're tempering expectations given the inherent volatility in late-season matchups.

The 62% confidence level reflects strong fundamentals without overextending into uncertain territory. This is exactly the type of edge we want to exploit: measurable, defensible, and backed by multiple convergent indicators.
